Commentary.Commentary: 235 is the target for New Zealand to take a 2-1 lead in the series. Do they have the arsenal to chase this down? No Ross Taylor while Kane Williamson is out of form. Who sticks his hand up tonight? Stay tuned for the answer...

Decent bowling from New Zealand. They never allowed the visitors to get away and even during the Morgan-Stokes stand, they kept things under control. Colin de Grandhomme was the most surprising factor, registering his most economical figures in a 10-over spell, reading 10-1-24-1. Ish Sodhi got some beating but picked up the key wickets of Bairstow, Stokes and Buttler - the latter two, when they were going big.

Considering that Eoin Morgan was looking to bat till the end, one would say that Ben Stokes should have stayed on after his captain got out. But England were focussed more on getting quick runs and though they did get a few, they will feel they are 20-30 runs short. No batsman scored a fifty, which shows that this is not a track where a batsman is set.

Lack of quick runs on a sticky track resulted in the early dismissal of Jason Roy but then Joe Root threw his wicket away. New Zealand then came back with the scalp of Jonny Bairstow before the 71-run stand between Eoin Morgan and Ben Stokes stalled them. During this stand, it seemed like 250-plus was on the cards but the skipper's wicket opened the floodgates.

A total which will keep both the teams happy. New Zealand would have aimed to restrict England under 250 while the visiting side will feel that even 235 is not going to be that easy to be chased down. Only disappointment would be the soft dismissals.

OUT! A run out to end the innings. Third one tonight. Full on middle, Curran swings it wide of long on and comes back for the second. Henry Nicholls attacks the ball and returns a good throw to Boult who takes the bails off. No chance for Wood to make it back in time. ENGLAND HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 234!
Yorker outside off, dug out towards cover for one more.
Outside off, Mark swings but makes no connection with wood.
Full on middle, Curran backs away to the leg side and drives it down to long on for a single.
Mark Wood is the last man in.

OUT! BULL'S EYE! What an athlete, is Trent Boult. Superb bowler, magnificent fielder as well. First he bowls a sharp bouncer as a response to the boundary Rashid hit on the previous ball. The batsman swings but is early and misses. Is hit bang on the helmet. Curran calls Rashid through for a single but he has barely left his crease. Boult quickly gets to the ball, picks it up, turns around, takes aim and boom. Right at the base of the stumps at the non-striker's end. Rashid is nowhere in the frame.
FOUR! Fine start to the over! Full and outside off, Rashid backs away and steers this behind point for a boundary!
The batsman drives this through the covers. One run added to the total. 7 runs and a run out from that over, Southee finishes with figures of 10-0-48-1.
FOUR! That is a terrific shot. Full on middle, Rashid whips a la helicopter style, over square leg and gets a boundary.
Tom Curran walks in at number 10, replacing Moeen Ali.

OUT! Moeen is run out. Another set batsman falls. Nothing Rashid could do over here. A bit of his mistake, as he whips this full ball towards short mid-wicket and as a habit, takes off for the single. Moeen responds and over-commits. He is already halfway down the track but then Rashid stands still. No chance for Moeen to come back as Colin de Grandhomme lobs a throw to the bowler who does the rest.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, Adil drives it through the covers. He sets off for the second but is turned down at the right time. Good call because Rashid has to dive in at the bowler's end.
Excellent yorker, Rashid can only dig it out.
Full and outside off, eased wide of long off for a brace. 5 runs and a wicket from that over, Boult has figures of 9-1-40-2. 9 runs have come in the last 2 overs for England.
A short ball now, Ali looks to pull but misses once more.
Full and wide outside off, Ali slashes but misses.

Outside off, steered through point for a single.

OUT! Number 7 falls and the previous over has resulted in a wicket. A low full toss, on middle, Woakes backs away and looks to go over the top but cannot get it past Kane Williamson at wide mid off. Simple catch and that breaks the quickfire stand. Woakes smiles after looking at Moeen, signalling that he tried to get it wider.
Terrific over. A low full toss to finish, pushed down to long off for only a single. Only 4 singles from that over.
Excellent fielding. A low full toss, on middle, Woakes backs away and drills it through the covers but cannot get it past Martin Guptill over there who dives to his right to stop the ball.

FOUR! In the gap! Very useful runs for England and they are coming at a quick pace. A short ball, around off, Moeen looks to pull but is hurried into the shot. Miscues his pull and it goes high in the air but luckily for him, it trisects three people - point running to his right, sweeper cover to his left and cover running back!

FOUR! Superb batting. On a length outside off, Woakes waits for the ball to come to him and dabs it past the keeper to the third man fence. 200 UP FOR ENGLAND. 260 looks a possibility now.

OUT! It is not a stumping but still a wicket. Buttler has edged it. Beautiful bowling from Sodhi again and he has three now. Full and outside off, Buttler tries to repeat the shot which fetched him a six earlier in the over, aiming to go inside out but this time he is a bit too far from the ball. He misses and his back leg is dragged out of the crease. Tom Latham collects and then whips off the bails, and then appeals. To the naked eye it looks like a stumping but replays show that his back foot is in. They check for the no ball which is fine as well. Buttler walks back shaking his head. It is not against the decision. Perhaps the shot he played. Snickometer detects a fat edge. Big wicket again.
STUMPED? Definitely looks so. Has been referred upstairs...
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
Good comeback from the bowler, lands it on middle, drags his length back a bit, Jos goes back but is cramped for room as he tries to work it to the leg side, Hits it back to the bowler.
SIX! Inside out. What a shot. Tossed up outside off, Buttler gives himself room to the leg side and lofts it over cover for a biggie.
Full on middle, Moeen slogs it through mid-wicket for a single. The stand moves to 10 from 10 balls.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
FOUR! WALLOP! Dragged short, Buttler pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary!

OUT! Stokes holes out now! Smart bowling from Sodhi and he has his second. Stokes makes a trigger movement just before Sodhi releases the ball, moving to the leg side. The leggie sees that and fires it wide outside off. Stokes now has to reach out to go over the top and mistimes it towards long off where Colin Munro takes a good judgemental catch near the ropes. Cannot blame Stokes for going big but can be critical, given that he should have stayed till the end, now that Morgan is not there. Fighting innings comes to an end.
Landed around off, eased through the covers for a run.
Very full, pushed down to long off for a single.

The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Full on middle, pushed wide of long on for a single.

SHANE WARNE unearthed! What a ball. Almost like the ball of the 20th century which got rid of Mike Gatting. Superb ball. Sodhi tosses this outside leg and Buttler stays back to defend. But the ball lands, then spins away a mile past the bat. Poor Buttler has no chance, misses it completely and so does Tom Latham behind. Colin de Grandhomme dives to his left from slip but even he cannot stop that! Two byes taken.

DRINKS are on the field. Just the kind of lift New Zealand needed. They have not been bowling badly but were struggling to break the stubborn stand between Morgan and Stokes. Also, England were looking to break free and this wicket will now keep them quiet for a few overs.

Southee is pumped up and New Zealand sense an opening. Fine innings from Morgan and that is a big wicket with the skipper looking to play anchor.

Huge shout! Looks close but Sodhi does not think so. Full and outside off, Morgan comes forward to defend but misses and is hit on the pads. In my opinion, that could have been reviewed but my colleague Milind, who himself is a right-arm medium pacer, reckons that the impact was outside off. I dare not argue with him, considering that he competes well with the Hawk Eye, eyeing things like a hawk, but still, would like an official confirmation. Still waiting...
Full on middle, chipped uppishly towards long on for a single to get off the mark straightaway.
Ben Stokes is in now, at number 5, replacing Bairstow.

OUT! Googled by the googly! Sodhi has struck in his second over. He tosses this one outside off and Bairstow fails to read the wrong 'un. Looks to drive against the turn, thinking that it will spin in. Misses and the ball hits the middle stump. Fine, fine ball and we now have two fairly new men in the middle.
Works this through the leg side for a run.

New Zealand coach Mike Hesson is on the sidelines. He says that the pitch looks spongy with a bit of extra bounce. Is not quite sure what a good total is on this surface. On Mark Chapman, Hesson is confident that the young lad has got a big role to play for New Zealand in the coming future. Reckons that it will be difficult for batsmen to play the new balls and wants his side to save boundaries.
FOUR! Lucky. Full and on middle and leg, Morgan gets down and reverse sweeps it over short third man for a boundary.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.

DRINKS are on the field. An absorbing hour of cricket. This pitch is certainly not the easiest to bat on and grafting is the way to go here. England have plenty of stroke-makers and they are finding it difficult to adjust. Credit to the batsmen for being patient so far but that is slowly dimishing, with plenty of shots being played in the latter half of that hour.
Full and outside off, pushed towards mid off. Fine over from de Grandhomme, apart from that boundary ball.
Now the skipper dances down the track and pushes it to point.

Outside off, on a length, shouldered arms to. 4 runs and a wicket from that over, de Grandhomme has started well today - 2-0-5-1 so far.
WIDE. Full and down the leg side, Morgan misses his flick.

OUT! That is a good catch but was that shot necessary? Root stands there in despair. Being aggressive is fine but trying to be ultra-aggressive is just not Root's area. He has tried to do something out of the ordinary to lift the run-rate and in the process, gifted his wicket. A length ball, in line of the stumps, nothing dangerous, Root jumps down the track and tries to do something fancy. Aims to go over mid on but skews it off the inner half. There is just one fielder inside the circle on the leg side and it is Ish Sodhi at wide mid on. The ball travels quickly to him but the leggie reacts well, taking a decent catch. A meter either side of Sodhi and it would have been a boundary. But was that shot needed? A kind of cameo is not quite expected from Root.

Outside off, on a length, Jonny feels for it but misses.
Played to the point region by the batsman.

Beautiful ball. On a length outside off, coming in a long way, Bairstow is caught in his crease as he looks to flick and is hit on the pads. The ball deflects behind and Tom Latham dives to his right to collect. Southee appeals but umpire Palliyaguruge is calm. Height was the factor.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.

FOUR! Second of the over. This time Roy goes over. A length ball, outside off, Roy lofts this over the infield over cover and finds the boundary.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
FOUR! MARVELLOUS! That is a fantastic shot. Full and outside off, Roy leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary.
On a good length, just around off and outside off, watchfully defended.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, swinging in, Bairstow somehow manages to push it to mid on.

TOP EDGE, SAFE! Lucky, lucky escape for Jonny Bairstow. On a length on middle, Bairstow looks to tuck but gets a top edge. Boult is a bit slow to react and by the time he runs to catch the ball, he is late.
Trent Boult to bowl with the second new ball.

We are all set for the game to begin. Jason Roy and Jonny Bairstow are the openers for England. Tim Southee to start off proceedings for New Zealand. Roy to face. Here we go...

Now Trent Boult is having a chat with Craig Cummins. The fast bowler looks confident ahead of this clash. Is enjoying his form at the moment, admitting being under the pump in the T20Is. Does not review himself too much, he says and smiles. Adds that he just looks to stick to the basics in every match and is enjoying his cricket at the moment. On performing when the ball is swinging, Boult says that as a fast bowler, the challenge is not to rely on the ball swinging and just bowl consistent line and length. States that on a given day, New Zealand are good enough to beat England. Further says that there are different challenges - different grounds, different pitches and different balls reacting differently to different surfaces. And of course, different oppositions as well.

Adil Rashid is having a chat with Nasser Hussain. Feels England played exceptionally well in the second ODI, restricting the Kiwis to 200-odd on a good pitch. On the fielding, he says that they were not doing anything special, just sticking to basics, practicing hard and improving their mindset. On his own mindset as a leggie, he says that his main aim is to pick wickets, nothing different from others. On smaller grounds in New Zealand, Rashid admits it is a challenge to bowl on such grounds and it comes down to mind games in the end.

PITCH REPORT - This is being done by Craig Cummins. He says that it is a hard pitch to define. There is a bit of dead grass right in the middle of the surface but nice and dry. Next to it, is a bit of a wet patch and going further aside, there is some nicely rolled grass. He adds, while the surface does not look great to look, it is great underneath.

England captain, Eoin Morgan, admits that this does not look like the prettiest of pitches to be coming across and would have chosen to bowl as well. Predominantly to make use of the pitch first up with the ball. Informs that Mark Wood comes in place of David Willey and they have gone for extra pace simply becaue there will be no sideways movement. Hopes that his side performs well tonight and goes 2-1 up.

New Zealand skipper, Kane Williamson says that it looks an interesting surface and is pretty hard. Informs that he is playing an extra bowler in Ish Sodhi in place of Lockie Ferguson. On his own fitness, he says he is fine and feels nice to come back. Agrees that he is a straight swap for Ross Taylor who should be fit for the next game. Admits that New Zealand were not a 100 percent in the second ODI and looks for an improved performance tonight.
TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin now. Kane Williamson flips it, Heads is the call from Eoin Morgan, but it is tails. NEW ZEALAND OPT TO CHASE.

WEATHER - Rain and New Zealand are never far apart. However, as of now, bright, sunny and cloudless skies welcome us to the Westpac Stadium. Hopefully, we get a full game of cricket uninterrupted by rain.

If it was an abject England display in the first ODI, they roared back in the second to level the series 1-1. We now have a 3-match series and depending on which team shapes up better, that unit is poised to win the series. Who will it be? Hello and a warm welcome to the third ODI between New Zealand and England at the Westpac Stadium, Wellington.
